key_insight: Active learning makes interatomic-potential training more data-efficient by selecting reference calculations relevant to intended simulation conditions.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive training can better align atomistic models with engineering applications spanning alloy mechanics, ion diffusion, functional materials, and reactive systems.
method: Iterate candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating.
Acquire configurations using committee disagreement, Gaussian-process uncertainty, or pretrained-model representations.
Tailor sampling to on-the-fly dynamics, model fine-tuning, or far-from-equilibrium reactions.
evidence_signal: The review surveys more than 70 studies, emphasizing 2020–2026, but the abstract reports no pooled quantitative benchmark of accuracy or data savings.
watch_item: Uncertainty estimates are architecture-dependent and may be least reliable on the unfamiliar configurations where accurate acquisition matters most.
paper_title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
